title: Microsoft 365 admin center: Copilot Credits usage report for pay-as-you-go in Copilot Chat
summary: Hold: the licensing field says entitlement is not yet published, although Microsoft documents the pay-as-you-go prerequisite for this report. The admin paths, API calls, default state and rollout dates are supported; the licensing field needs to distinguish the known consumption model from the absence of a separate report price.

claims.claim: The Credits report is reached in the Microsoft 365 admin center through Reports > Usage > Reports > Microsoft Copilot > Credits.
claims.quote: In the navigation menu, select Reports. If you don't see Reports, select Show all, and then select Reports. ... Select Usage. ... On the Usage page, under Reports, select Microsoft Copilot, and then select Credits.

claims.claim: No API for the Copilot Chat Credits report itself is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Credits report" "API"; Microsoft Graph reports Microsoft Copilot Credits report get usage report metered Chat. Read Credits report, Graph usage reports, Copilot usage API excerpts and Cost Management API; none documents this report's API.

claims.claim: Name concealment is configured in the Microsoft 365 admin center at Settings > Org settings > Services > Reports > Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.
claims.quote: select Settings. ... Select Org Settings. ... On the Services tab, select Reports. ... In the Reports panel, uncheck the checkbox next to Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.

claims.claim: PATCH /beta/admin/reportSettings updates the tenant's report name-concealment setting.

claims.claim: The tenant-wide report concealment setting applies to this report.
claims.quote: By default, user-specific information like usernames, display names, groups, and sites is hidden in usage reports. To learn how to display this information in usage reports, see Show user, group, or site details in usage reports.

claims.claim: Setting the request-body property displayConcealedNames to true conceals user, group and site names.
claims.quote: displayConcealedNames ... If set to true, all reports conceal user information such as usernames, groups, and sites.

claims.claim: Setting displayConcealedNames to false shows identifiable names.
claims.quote: If false, all reports show identifiable information.

claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version in Microsoft Graph are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: GET /beta/copilot/costManagement/usageReports/userUsageRecords?startDate={startDate}&endDate={endDate} retrieves per-user credit consumption.
claims.quote: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/usageReports/userUsageRecords?startDate=2026-07-01&endDate=2026-07-02&$orderby=consumedQuantity desc&$top=2&$count=true

claims.quote: The range must select exactly one completed UTC day. Current-day, future, and multi-day ranges are rejected, not clamped.

claims.claim: The listed per-user Cost Management call is not an equivalent of the Copilot Chat Credits report.
claims.quote: Get a list of costManagementUserUsageRecord objects that report each user's consumption of Copilot Credits for one completed UTC day, ranked by consumption.

claims.claim: The listed per-user call is not an equivalent of every Consumption tab breakdown.
claims.quote: Get a list of costManagementUserUsageRecord objects that report each user's consumption of Copilot Credits for one completed UTC day, ranked by consumption.

claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown, meaning Microsoft has not published how the feature is obtained.
claims.quote: After you set up pay-as-you-go for Microsoft Copilot Chat, either in the Microsoft 365 admin center or the Power Platform admin center, and enable agent usage in your organization, you see a new report that includes metrics for credits used.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to "consumption". Keep the notes' published pay-as-you-go prerequisite and the statement that MC1069563 requires no Microsoft Copilot license; retain the narrow statement that no separate report price is published. The model describes the pay-as-you-go scenario, not a charge for opening the report.
